notes: Correctness fix, not a performance change. Commit 5bcac20 introduced the tiled prefill kernel with a local `NEG: tl.constexpr = -1e30` and a stray edit replaced `-float('inf')` with `NEG` inside the unrelated `_paged_decode_kernel` above it. Triton resolves names at first launch, so the non-split decode path (n_seqs * n_qheads >= 128, i.e. ~16+ concurrent sequences on Gemma 4) raises NameError on CUDA; the CPU suite never launches a kernel and could not see it. Review of PR #3 traced that -inf cannot produce a NaN here: the per-sequence start_b/lo bounds guarantee every iterated block has at least one valid slot, matching the sibling prefill and split-K kernels which already use -inf. The regression test is static (AST free-name check over every @triton.jit function, no triton needed): verified failing at b61ba6f with {'_paged_decode_kernel': ['NEG']} and passing at the fix. GPU parity of the non-split decode path against split-K remains the review's outstanding ask; it needs a CUDA box and is recorded as not covered.
